back.hook: Dust is not the end. It is the staging ground of resurrection grace.
paragraphs: Of all the New Testament letters, 1 Peter lives closest to the ground. It was written to exiles and foreigners, a scattered people facing slander and a fiery trial, and it does not soften any of that. But in the same breath it says God has caused you to be born again to a living hope. Twelve weeks walk straight through the letter, chapter by chapter, from that new birth to the humility that waits on God's mighty hand.

Before Week One, “The Six Faces of the Dust” names what the psalmist meant by a soul clinging to dust -- frailty, humiliation, sin, worldliness, nearness to despair, and the dust God delights to revive -- so that whatever face your own dust wears, you know it is precisely the ground He stoops to reach. Ransomed from the futile ways handed down to you, called a living stone, and told that suffering is a little while but the glory is eternal, you are not too far down for this letter.
items: The full passage in the World English Bible
